🇳🇵 Nepal–Tibet Border Avalanche & Flood | 26 August 2026 A major ice–rock avalanche near the Nepal–Tibet border triggered a cascading hazard: a large glacier mass collapsed from high elevation, sending ice, rock and sediment into the Lhende Khola. The debris blocked the river and formed a temporary barrier lake, which then released a powerful downstream surge of muddy water, debris and boulders. 🌡️ Possible factors: glacier instability, melting ice, steep crevassed terrain, meltwater lubrication and possible seismic triggering. ⚠️ Some claims remain unconfirmed, so the exact trigger requires scientific investigation. 🌊 Avalanche → Debris Flow → River Blockage → Dam Breach → Flood #Nepal #NepalFlood #NepalLandslide #NepalAvalanche #NepalTibetBorder Himalayas HimalayanAvalanche Landslide GlacierCollapse GlacialLake BarrierLake FlashFlood DebrisFlow LhendeKhola Bhotekoshi ClimateChange GlacierMelt NaturalDisaster DisasterScience EarthScience 26August2026

More than 1,300 people are missing in Nepal and Tibet, including 47 Americans, after a glacial collapse caused catastrophic floods, with video showing mud sweeping through entire communities. Drone footage in Nepal showed roads destroyed and buildings buried by thundering water the color of wet cement. Nepalese authorities ramped up operations in the worst-affected districts of Nuwakot and Rasuwa. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet is not a one-off. The Lhende Khola river system has now flooded twice in just 14 months and the increasingly unstable Himalayan ice system threatens communities, infrastructure and water supplies across one of the world’s most densely populated regions. The region saw similar flash floods in August last year, when a glacial lake in Tibet overflowed because of high temperatures. Nine people were killed, and critical infrastructure, including a bridge connecting Nepal and China, was damaged.

videos.caption: It’s hard to fully grasp just how devastating the floods and mudslides have been in Nuwakot, Nepal. Seeing the level of destruction firsthand really puts the scale of the disaster into perspective. The size of the initial wave compared to a person is terrifying. It’s clear that supporting people as they return to their communities and rebuild their lives will be a long process. The work ahead will be hard and will take time, but our team is there to continue to support these communities, especially the children who have been so deeply affected.

They say Nepal isn’t safe… but Nepal is OPEN. 🇳🇵❤️ The mountains are still standing. The people are still smiling. The spirit of Nepal is still alive. Our doors are open, and we’re waiting to welcome you. Come see Nepal with your own eyes. 🏔️🙏 Visit Nepal. Nepal is Open. 🇳🇵 #CapCut #N#NepalV#VisitNepalN#NepalIsOpenT#TravelNepal #NepalTourism
